content.text: All preferred elements are present across §§ 13.1–13.3; no redline needed.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: The licence package meets our preferred position in full. § 13.1 grants the subscription right to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf"; § 13.2 grants Customer and its Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable" fully paid licence for paid-up software and Vendor Technology (extended to Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables by § 14.3); and § 13.3 limits Vendor revocation or suspension to a material uncured breach after notice and a cure opportunity, and permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by § 24 (which allows Customer assignment to a merger/acquisition successor without Vendor consent). Affiliate coverage is automatic in the grant, so no written-notice mechanic is needed. Noted, not flagged here: the revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence in § 14.2 conflicts with this package; that is a Deliverable ownership/licence issue addressed under the IP rule and we do not double-flag it.
